authors_year: Mainsant, Larose, Brönnimann, Jongmans, Michoud, Jaboyedoff (2012)
target_process: Pre-failure velocity drop preceding catastrophic earthslide-earthflow; clay softening / pore-pressure rise
components: Vertical / surface-wave (Rayleigh) cross-correlation between sensor pairs
depth_sensitivity: Velocity change localized at base of sliding layer (shallow, a few m) from frequency-dependent analysis
dvv_amplitude: ~-7% surface-wave velocity drop over several days before the Aug 2010 failure (reported elsewhere as ~6% for the event)
best_practice_note: Foundational landslide dv/v study; demonstrated days-ahead precursor on a clayey landslide using short-distance sensor pairs and high-frequency surface waves

target_process: Water-table / seasonal hydrology monitoring in a deep-seated slow-moving clayey landslide
region_site: Avignonet / Mas d'Avignonet landslide, Trièves (French Alps), France
depth_sensitivity: Rayleigh sensitivity peaks ~2-3 m depth in 6-8 Hz band, tracking shallow water table
dvv_amplitude: Seasonal dv/v of order 1% (anti-correlated with water table)
best_practice_note: Shows dv/v tracks water table in deep-seated slow landslide; choose frequency band so Rayleigh depth sensitivity matches expected water-table depth

authors_year: Bièvre, Franz, Larose, Carrière, Jongmans, Jaboyedoff (2018)
target_process: Influence of environmental parameters (temperature, precipitation) on dv/v in a clayey mudflow; seasonal reversible variations vs precursor
components: Surface-wave cross-correlation; three pairs of sensors
freq_band_hz: ~5-15 (surface-wave band; reported sensitivity to shallow layer <=2 m)
depth_sensitivity: Shallow (~2 m or less); ~30-day lag between air temperature and dv/v
dvv_amplitude: Seasonal reversible dv/v smaller than the ~6% pre-failure drop of 2010
uncertainty_treatment: Correlation coefficient; seasonal-cycle modeling to separate from precursors
best_practice_note: Quantifies seasonal/thermal dv/v cycles that must be removed before precursor detection; ~30-day temperature lag locates sensitivity in the top ~2 m

authors_year: Fiolleau, Jongmans, Bièvre, Chambon, Baillet, Vial (2020)
target_process: Pre-rupture monitoring of a clay-block failure; combined dv/v and resonance-frequency precursors
region_site: Harmalière landslide, French Western Alps (collapsed Nov 2016)
freq_band_hz: 1-12 (monitoring); dv/v in 2-4 and 8-10 bands; block resonance ~9-16
stack_scheme: Hourly records, daily averaging vs reference
dvv_amplitude: dv/v up to +/-10% at high frequency before rupture
uncertainty_treatment: Correlation-coefficient degradation tracked across bands; multi-parameter precursor timing
best_practice_note: Combine dv/v with resonance frequency; precursors appear at different times in different bands, so multi-band monitoring improves confidence

authors_year: Le Breton, Bontemps, Guillemot, Baillet, Larose (2021)
target_process: Review of ambient-noise dv/v for landslide monitoring; precursors, seasonal effects, spurious-fluctuation challenges
region_site: Global review (9 landslides monitored to date)
components: Cross-correlation of station pairs (and single-station variants discussed)
coda_window_s: end of direct waves to 5-10 periods (site-dependent)
depth_sensitivity: Shallow (meters to tens of m), set by high-frequency surface-wave sensitivity
dvv_amplitude: Pre-failure drops of several % on clayey landslides; seasonal cycles ~1%
uncertainty_treatment: Weaver et al. (2011) rms + SD over pairs/windows; discard CC<0.6
best_practice_note: Authoritative synthesis: confirms precursor ability on clayey landslides; stresses separating environmental/seasonal dv/v and checking for artifacts

target_process: Rainfall- and earthquake-driven dv/v; rigidity loss during M>=5 quakes and inhibited healing by rain/small quakes
region_site: Maca slow-moving Andean landslide, southern Peru (3-yr dataset)
components: Cross-correlation of station pairs; ambient noise plus local earthquakes
dvv_amplitude: dv/v drops below -1.2%; short-term -dv/v with 2-5 day lag after rain
best_practice_note: Demonstrates coupled rain+earthquake forcing; timing between forcings controls healing - monitor both triggers jointly

target_process: Shear-wave velocity structure / time-spatial Vs changes of flysch prone to mass movement
region_site: Just-Tęgoborze landslide, Carpathian flysch, southern Poland
stack_scheme: Cross-correlation / interferometric stacks; dispersion inversion (neighbourhood algorithm)
depth_sensitivity: Few m to tens of m (3-D Vs model of landslide body)
dvv_amplitude: n/r (focus on Vs structure / time-spatial Vs changes, not % dv/v)
best_practice_note: Shows high-frequency noise interferometry images Vs of flysch landslides; dense arrays + dispersion inversion give spatial structure

authors_year: Colombero, Baillet, Comina, Jongmans, Larose, Valentin, Vinciguerra (2018)
target_process: Temperature-controlled long-term evolution of a prone-to-fall cliff; reversible vs irreversible dv/v and resonance
region_site: Madonna del Sasso cliff, NW Italian Alps (Orta Lake), Italy
depth_sensitivity: ~tens of m (temperature reference at ~20 m borehole)
dvv_amplitude: Annual dv/v +/-10% at 2-4 Hz; ~+/-5% at higher frequencies
uncertainty_treatment: Correlation coefficient (~0.9 at low freq) as reliability metric
best_practice_note: For rock cliffs, distinguish reversible thermal dv/v from irreversible precursors; track both dv/v and resonance frequency

target_process: Earthflow dynamics from Rayleigh-wave velocity; velocity drop with acceleration and recovery with deceleration
freq_band_hz: n/a (active-source ReMi/MASW dispersion, not coda dv/v)
dvv_amplitude: Substantial Rayleigh-velocity drop on acceleration, slow recovery on deceleration
best_practice_note: Rayleigh-velocity changes track earthflow kinematics; combining passive interferometry with active MASW cross-validates

authors_year: Guillemot, Helmstetter, Larose, Baillet, Garambois, Mayoraz, Delaloye (2020)
target_process: Freeze-thaw control of dv/v on an unstable alpine slope (rock glacier); active-layer rigidity changes + microseismicity
region_site: Gugla rock glacier, Valais, Switzerland (3+ yr)
depth_sensitivity: Upper ~10 m (active layer 0-4.5 m, upper permafrost 4.5-10 m) for 4-14 Hz
best_practice_note: Use multiple 4-Hz sub-bands to depth-resolve freeze-thaw; higher bands = shallower; rigorous Weaver-style uncertainty

target_process: In-situ rock-slope destabilization; near-real-time precursor dv/v drop minutes before slope failure
dvv_amplitude: ~-0.5% precursor dv/v drop ~40 min before destabilization
best_practice_note: Demonstrates short-timescale (minutes) precursor; needs high temporal resolution and instability checks for early warning

authors_year: Liu, Li, Liang, Zhang, Jiang, Huang (2025)
target_process: High-resolution 4-D imaging of rainfall infiltration via noise-based dv/v; diurnal and rain-driven changes
region_site: Xishan Village landslide, Sichuan Province, China
stack_scheme: 20-min interval CCFs vs reference (SNR>4 wave-packet selection)
depth_sensitivity: Rainfall infiltration to ~8 m resolved; 15 m (15 Hz) to 40 m (5 Hz)
best_practice_note: Dense array + multi-frequency dv/v yields 4-D depth-time infiltration imaging; high station count enables spatial resolution

target_process: Moisture-driven elastic changes in a slow-moving clay-rich landslide; seasonal soil-moisture control on dv/v / surface-wave velocity
region_site: Hollin Hill Landslide Observatory, North Yorkshire, UK (2-yr)
stack_scheme: Time-lapse interferometry + MASW between recording periods
dvv_amplitude: Seasonal velocity variation linked to soil moisture/saturation (qualitative)
best_practice_note: Dense 10-station array across hydrogeological zones; saturation controls elastic properties - couple with moisture/H-V data

target_process: Pre-failure dv/v on an open-pit mine slope; subsurface precursor ahead of surface deformation
depth_sensitivity: Subsurface slope (dense borehole geophone array beneath slope)
dvv_amplitude: Velocity decrease ~12 days before slope-failure initiation
uncertainty_treatment: Decorrelation/CC; comparison with radar surface deformation
best_practice_note: Borehole/buried arrays detect subsurface precursors before surface (radar) signs; promising for early warning in engineered slopes
